You wake up and feel a tickle in your throat. Your head hurts. You’re mildly annoyed as you get the kids ready for school and dress for work yourself. Meanwhile, an epic war is being fought, just below your skin. Millions are fighting and dying for you to be able to complain as you head out the door.  
  
But most of us never really stop to ask: What even _is_ our immune system?  
  
Second only to the human brain in its complexity, it is one of the oldest and most critical facets of life on Earth. Without it, you would die within days. [NancyJ (nancyjjj) | 11553 comments](https://www.goodreads.com/user/show/68718060-nancyj "NancyJ (nancyjjj) | 11553 comments") First I need to say - if you want to strengthen your immune system, this book won't help you. The reason why, is the most interesting thing I learned from this book. More on that in a minute. I was hoping to gain some practical information to improve my health, control my allergies, deal with autoimmune, and maybe persuade my youngest to get vaccinated. My expectations were not met, at all, but I can't give the book a really low rating because it kept me engaged long enough to read the whole book.  
  
If you want to learn about the biology of the immune system, and the names of all the different types of cells and substances involved, this book or audio is a good choice. The language and narration is very upbeat and somewhat humorous. It's hard to be funny when describing cells, dendrites, neutrophils, bacteria, viruses, etc., but he does his best with metaphors. analogies and little stories. (Most are connected to soldiers, animals, wars, or blowing up stuff, so if you have a 10 year old who wants to be a doctor some day, get this audio.) I can't recall which cell or process was compared to a cute little bunny, a dumb soldier, or a crazy monkey with a machine gun, but I can tell you that the crazy monkey with a machine gun is the reason that you should NOT want a strong immune system. Two examples of a strong overreactive immune system: 1)A person dies from anaphylactic shock after being stung by a bee. 2) Auto-immune disorders, when your immune system attacks your own cells. This is "when things go very very wrong" as the author frequently repeated.  
  
The only practical advice for how to improve your immune system is to save your money on expensive supplements, powders, snake oil, or the latest thing someone is selling online. Also, eat a decent diet, learn to manage your reaction to stress, and move around so the cells in your immune system can get where they need to go. I'm not sure he even mentioned drinking fluids.
